I understand that it could fall within Rule 90(E) and I think it's a legitimate invocation of that objection, but we would ask the Chamber to proceed to order him to answer with the provision that it would not be used again him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We don't take a position on this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me just make two quick points, Mr. President, in line with the practice that seems to have developed around these issues. Number one, I -- I don't know whether the Court considers that it's necessary for the witness himself to invoke. I will say I have seen at least one proceeding in which a chamber permitted counsel to invoke on behalf of the witness who acquiesced. On the other hand, I have seen proceedings where the witness himself was required to invoke. I simply raise that. Secondly, if the Court does proceed in that direction, I would simply note that it has been our practice thus far to go into private session for responses to questions for which -- to which the witness has been compelled, and I simply wanted to remind the Chamber of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, do you like to add anything to Mr. Tieger's observation that we need to go into private session if the Chamber is to compel the witness to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I understood correctly, my learned friend, Mr. Tieger, from the -- from the Prosecution, it is the practice, I believe he said, of the Trial Chamber to move in -- in private session when it compels the witness to -- to answer the question. To my knowledge, there is no reason for us to go into -- into private session on this particular question. But if that is the -- the practice of the Trial Chamber, I would take no position on that, in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The ground or the reason for going into private session may be the protection in order that -- that is, in order to protect the witness for any potential use by any court. But, Mr. Tieger, do you like that add anything, having heard Mr. Zecevic's observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may say, Your Honours, I believe the protection which is guaranteed by the 90(E) and by the Chamber's decision is more than enough. I -- I don't think that -- that giving the -- the testimony in the private session will -- will necessarily help considerably the -- the -- that situation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, can you assist with us Mr. Tieger's first point that the objection should come from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I believe, since I'm representing the witness at this proceedings, I believe that I'm entitled to -- to -- to raise objection at -- at the point where the Defence finds that -- that the -- that the potential question is -- is perhaps the question which might intimidate the witness. It doesn't -- normally it wouldn't be expected of a witness to be that sophisticated in a legal sense to be able to distinguish whether a certain question might or might not intimidate him, especially knowing that each and every witness is under certain duress when he is taking the stand. Therefore, in my sincere opinion, I respectively say that it is quite appropriate for the Defence to take the objection on this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I have been quiet about the publish session because I have -- sensing the way the wind is blowing, but if you are thinking of going into private session, we would like to be heard on that before you do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you proceed now, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, as I think you well know, Mr. Tieger's reference to "our practice" is only limited to one instance in which Colonel Beara -- we initially went into private session and then afterward we unsealed all of that testimony finding that it was not necessary, so I think any reference to the practice is probably more in favour of the open session than a private session. But in any event, given the information in the statement, we can anticipate what the answers to these questions are going to be and I don't think there is any realistic prospect of him being prosecuted by some authority in some country where the Court's Rule 90(E) might not apply which would be really the only reason for going into private session. So I think in balance, the Chamber should maintain this evidence which is of public interest in the public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I also note, Mr. Robinson, in case of Mr. Beara, counsel for Mr. Beara wanted to hear his evidence, answer to the question in private session. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just two quick points. First of all, Mr. Robinson is -- is correct in one sense, we don't have a long-standing practice with respect to this. These issues have arisen fairly recently. But I would submit that the practice with respect to the precisely relevant circumstances outweighs any practice we've had with regard to totally inapposite circumstances in the past. However having said that, I was about to mention something along the lines that the Court did, and that was that when this issue came up about rendering the Beara testimony public, of course, one of the primary considerations in our acquiescence in that was the Defence position on that subject. And the view that if the witness and his counsel considered that that is the way they wanted to go, that any additional potential protections didn't need to be forced on them. They had chosen their path. And we would certainly acquiesce in that. If that is the circumstances that we have here obviously we would consider that a relevant consideration along the same lines, as we did in the Beara situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, the Court is minded to adjourn for today and will give its ruling first things tomorrow. Mr. Stanisic, while you can consult your counsel as to just general legal matters, but I'd like to advise you not to discuss about your testimony with anybody else, with anyone, including your counsel. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just for the sake of the record, I misspoke in my last -- last submission and instead of saying "incriminate," I used "intimidate." And it's on pages 94, line 18 and 21. I'm sorry. So it should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be corrected, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hearing is adjourned.
